title: Otis Digital Eco-system
subtitle: Building a centralized digital platform for customer self-service
context: Otis clients manage complex properties globally, but the legacy infrastructure made real-time equipment monitoring nearly impossible — leading to reactive maintenance, more downtime, and customer friction. As Lead Designer, I was tasked with turning a rigid, on-premise legacy system into a scalable, cloud-native ecosystem, balancing usability against strict regulatory compliance and technical debt while directing a team of two designers.
team: 2 UI Designers, 10+ Engineers, 1 Product Manager, 1 Project Manager
problemStatement: A fragmented legacy system prevented real-time equipment monitoring, forcing global clients into costly, reactive maintenance cycles and limiting Otis's ability to scale cloud-based services. The hypothesis: real-time health data and predictive alerts could reduce emergency repair calls by 20% and lift customer satisfaction.

challenges.title: Bridging the Technical Gap
challenges.desc: Providing "power user" tools for technical experts without overwhelming non-technical stakeholders.

challenges.title: Design for "High-Stakes" Compliance
challenges.desc: Balancing user-centricity with rigid safety and data regulations.

challenges.title: Scaling for Global Diversity
challenges.desc: Creating a "universal" system that still respects local market nuances.

sections.title: Process
sections.text: A phased approach: discovery to find quick UX wins and low-risk improvements, then validating solutions through user testing and workflow cleanup. We piloted the "Ask Otis" AI copilot to gather real-world feedback while defining a longer-term vision for AI-driven insights, energy prediction, and end-to-end optimization.

sections.title: On-Site Discovery
sections.text: Contextual inquiries at high-traffic NYC sites revealed a disconnect: the team was designing for "efficiency," but users were operating from "fear." Property managers felt real consequence-anxiety — afraid of a catastrophic error like shutting down an entire elevator bank — so they offloaded even simple tasks to Otis engineers.

sections.title: Defining User Archetypes
sections.text: Field research distilled into two personas around a core tension — action vs. oversight. Field Engineers need high-density, action-oriented workflows for rapid diagnostics; Building Managers need a guided experience built around psychological safety and confidence.

points.title: Building Manager
points.desc: Non-technical daily user managing operations and tenant communication. Needs simple guided workflows, plain-language labels, and confirmation before committing changes.

points.title: Field Engineer
points.desc: Highly technical, occasional user diagnosing issues on-site. Needs real-time status, fast access to actionable data, and predictable workflows with minimal friction.

sections.title: Mitigating Risk
sections.text: Rapid prototyping bridged stakeholder requirements and user needs, with iterative testing inside active sprint cycles to de-risk "quick win" initiatives and keep decisions grounded in real usage rather than assumptions.

sections.title: Testing Outcome
sections.text: Testing confirmed the psychological-safety focus worked — cutting task time by 70% and error rates by 45%. The platform shifted from a cumbersome chore to a high-velocity tool, giving users the confidence to handle routine maintenance without relying on Otis engineers.

features.title: Dashboard & AI Copilot
features.desc: A centralized dashboard with real-time service visibility, paired with the "Ask Otis" AI copilot to surface insights and guide next steps while keeping users in control.

features.title: Traffic Control & Monitoring
features.desc: Modular tools for security teams and engineers to manage calls, secure floors, and schedule elevator operations in real time.

features.title: Health & Energy
features.desc: AI-powered insights monitor elevator health and energy usage to surface early risks, predict maintenance needs, and find opportunities to cut energy consumption.

features.title: New User Guide
features.desc: A guided onboarding experience with contextual tutorials that shorten training time and build user confidence faster.

results.text: Cloud EMS 2.0 launched in early September, modernizing elevator management across 10+ core workflows and three user roles, and automating complex edge cases to reduce operational burden.
